stages.title: Fix & decide
stages.goal: Settle every inconsistency between your own documents before anyone else finds it.
stages.gate: You can say your career timeline and your education in one breath, you have chosen option A, B or C, and the R3/R13 decisions are made.

stages.title: The role & Leapfrog
stages.goal: Know exactly what the role asks for, where your proof lives, and what Leapfrog ships.
stages.gate: Name Leapfrog's four offerings with your parallel for each, and say the one-sentence reliability line from memory.

stages.title: Your narrative & stories
stages.goal: Rehearse the spoken parts aloud: intro, motivation, weakness, and the story bank.
stages.gate: Intro under 90 seconds without notes; S1–S5 told in STAR shape; [fill] items either filled or dropped.

stages.title: Project dossiers
stages.goal: Own every project you might be asked about, including its honest status.
stages.gate: 60-second pitch for P1, P2, P3 and P6 with no notes, and every number defensible.

stages.title: Technical Q&A
stages.goal: Answer in the shape: principle → implementation → trade-off → your proof.
stages.gate: Pick any five questions at random and answer each in 60–120 seconds with a project reference.

stages.title: AgentCore, Bedrock & design
stages.goal: Speak AgentCore fluently and draw the referral-intake design on paper.
stages.gate: D1 drawn in 5 minutes with three failure modes named before anyone asks.

stages.title: Code, culture & your questions
stages.goal: Have the coding protocol, C1 and the culture angles ready; choose what you will ask them.
stages.gate: Narrate C1 from memory and pick two or three questions from Part 12.

stages.title: Final run
stages.goal: One last rehearsal, logistics, and the one-page sheet.
stages.gate: Five mock questions aloud, every checklist item ticked, logged in by 12:50.

reference.title: Tech flow map
reference.kicker: Every library and framework, in build order
